newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on spinners' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on spinners' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Sunday on spinners' demand for a good quality cotton which was in short supply due to pest attack, dealers said.
Rates were likely to open higher on Monday due to the same factor and fear of lower production, dealer Nasim Usman said.
Crop estimates ranged between 8.5 million 375-lb and 8.8 million, he said. Government officials have not confirmed it.
In the kerb market, the rate for NIAB-78 ranged between 2,300 and 2,400 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the broker said. The rate for K-68 variety ranged between 2,550 and 2,575, Usman said.
